course_name_original: Intelligent systems of supply and protection
course_name_en: Intelligent systems of supply and protection

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the protection systems used in low voltage networks.
Knows the structure, principle of operation and application of basic electrical apparatus and current and voltage transformers.
Knows methods for improving power quality in low voltage networks.
Has knowledge regarding the power supply of modern light sources.
Knows the issues of island operation of autonomous energy sources.
Has knowledge regarding modern DC power supplies.
Can measure and assess the quality of electrical energy in single-phase systems.
Can indicate ways to improve power quality in low voltage supply systems.
Can select basic protections in low voltage networks.

syllabus_topics: Issues of power quality in low voltage networks (4 hours): Discussion of power quality issues in low voltage networks. Methods for improving power quality: power supplies with unity power factor, power electronic systems for improving power quality.

Single-phase photovoltaic system cooperating with the grid - laboratory exercise + knowledge test (5 hours): Demonstration and discussion of the operation of a single-phase grid-connected solar inverter powered by photovoltaic modules.
Single-phase power supply systems with increased power factor (PFC) - laboratory exercise + knowledge test (5 hours): Demonstration and discussion of the operation of a single-phase PFC power supply.
Advanced power supply and protection systems (4h).
Single-phase active rectifier-filter - laboratory exercise + knowledge test (5 hours): Demonstration and discussion of the operation of a single-phase parallel active rectifier-filter.
Problems related to the use of renewable energy sources (2 hours).
Powering and control of incandescent, discharge, and LED light sources (2 hours).
assessment_rules: To obtain a positive final grade, a positive grade from the laboratory is essential. The average of laboratory grades obtained in all terms is calculated. The final grade is determined based on the following dependency: if average > 4.75 then final grade := 5.0 else if average > 4.25 then final grade := 4.5 else if average > 3.75 then final grade := 4.0 else if average > 3.25 then final grade := 3.5 else final grade := 3. Attendance at lectures is not explicitly stated as obligatory, but students participate in classes to learn the teaching content. For laboratory classes, students perform exercises according to provided materials, are obliged to prepare for the exercise (verified by an oral or written colloquium), and must present a solution to the problem to pass.
